svg.title: B14 / PHOENIX INFILTRATION — Postfire Soil Recovery Observatory engineering mission profile
svg.desc: B14, PHOENIX INFILTRATION — Postfire Soil Recovery Observatory. Original project: Soil hydraulic properties three years after the Frye Fire on Mount Graham, Arizona. Session B: Earth & Environmental Engineering. Scientific question: What explains burned/unburned infiltration and repellency differences, and how do point measurements translate into storm runoff? Testable hypothesis: Litter/carbon and soil moisture may mediate contrasting responses; burn status alone should be incomplete, while rainfall intensity changes effective watershed parameters.. svg.text: Soil hydraulic properties three years after the Frye Fire on Mount Graham, Arizona
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Study three-year postfire hydraulics as heterogeneous recovery, without
presuming burned soil always infiltrates less. The historical abstract
reports the opposite direction in its sampled plots. Preserve that context
and test litter, carbon, severity and spatial scaling as explanations; the
abstract is not a replacement for raw measurements or new results.
What explains burned/unburned infiltration and repellency differences, and
how do point measurements translate into storm runoff?
